description: Per-control rules for mapping vulnerability and infrastructure (runtime-security / k8s-health) findings to compliance controls. Each rule defines a predicate that is evaluated against a mapping input. Multiple rules can match the same finding (a finding can map to multiple controls). Predicates are pure data, evaluated by the mapping-engine. Rules that predate the `subjectKind` discriminator (S6-4) are guarded with `subject_kind_is: vulnerability` so they only match vulnerability findings, exactly as before.

rules.title: Continuous Vulnerability Management
rules.description: Any CVE with severity >= Medium is in scope of CIS Control 7 (Continuous Vulnerability Management).

rules.title: Application Software Security
rules.description: Any CVE discovered through Software Composition Analysis (SCA) is in scope of CIS Control 16 (Application Software Security).

rules.title: Flaw Remediation
rules.description: All CVEs are subject to NIST SI-2 (Flaw Remediation). This is the default catch-all rule.

rules.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
rules.description: All CVEs detected by the platform's scanning are evidence of NIST RA-5 (Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning) operating.

rules.title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
rules.description: CVEs flagged as Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) — actively exploited in the wild — escalate to NIST SI-7 (Software/Firmware Integrity) for integrity-verification and emergency remediation.

rules.title: Developer Testing and Evaluation
rules.description: CVEs introduced into the codebase within the last 30 days imply a gap in NIST SA-11 (Developer Testing and Evaluation) — pre-commit and CI tests should have caught them.

rules.title: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software
rules.description: Privileged containers, root execution, dangerous capabilities, or a weak/missing SecurityContext are secure-configuration gaps in scope of CIS Control 4.

rules.title: Configuration Settings
rules.description: Privileged containers, root execution, dangerous capabilities, or a weak SecurityContext are configuration-settings deviations from the platform baseline (NIST CM-6).

rules.title: Least Privilege
rules.description: Privileged containers, root execution, dangerous capabilities, hostPath mounts, and risky ServiceAccount/RBAC bindings all grant more privilege than least-privilege (NIST AC-6) allows.

rules.title: Data Protection
rules.description: A hostPath volume mount can expose the node filesystem (and any data on it) to the container, in scope of CIS Control 3 (Data Protection).

rules.title: Boundary Protection
rules.description: A hostPath volume mount crosses the container/host boundary, in scope of NIST SC-7 (Boundary Protection).

rules.title: Access Control Management
rules.description: Pods using the default ServiceAccount or risky RBAC bindings are access-control-management gaps in scope of CIS Control 6.

rules.title: Account Management
rules.description: The `default` ServiceAccount and risky RBAC bindings are unmanaged/over-broad accounts in scope of NIST AC-2 (Account Management).

rules.title: Access Enforcement
rules.description: Risky ServiceAccount and RBAC bindings weaken the platform's access-enforcement guarantees (NIST AC-3).

rules.title: Inventory and Control of Software Assets
rules.description: A container image that is not pinned to a digest cannot be reliably inventoried or verified, in scope of CIS Control 2.

rules.title: Baseline Configuration
rules.description: An unpinned image tag can drift from the approved baseline image without detection (NIST CM-2).

rules.title: System Component Inventory
rules.description: A mutable image tag breaks the SBOM-based component inventory's ability to track exactly what is deployed (NIST CM-8).

rules.title: Denial-of-Service Protection
rules.description: A container with no CPU/memory limits can exhaust node resources, in scope of NIST SC-5 (Denial-of-Service Protection).

rules.title: System Monitoring
rules.description: CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, restart storms, node pressure, image pull failures, and unschedulable/pending/failed pods are workload-availability anomalies that NIST SI-4 (System Monitoring) is responsible for detecting.

rules.title: System Recovery and Reconstitution
rules.description: CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, and pending/failed/unschedulable pods require the platform to restore the workload to an operational state, in scope of NIST CP-10 (System Recovery and Reconstitution).

rules.title: Denial-of-Service Protection
rules.description: Restart storms, OOMKilled containers, and node pressure indicate resource exhaustion in scope of NIST SC-5 (Denial-of-Service Protection).

rules.title: Network Infrastructure Management
rules.description: A node reporting pressure or an unschedulable condition is an unmanaged piece of network/compute infrastructure, in scope of CIS Control 12.
